name: lyric-field-spacing
style: late-90s New York street rap, one heavyset MC who treats his verse like a bebop drum solo turned into words: rhythm played as melody, syllables dragged a hair behind the snare then let out patiently, stacked multisyllable rhymes rolling into each other, unbothered talking cadence, a deliberate beat of silence right before each punchline lands. Vocal: enormous man, low velvet chest baritone, lazy Brooklyn vowels, a short asthmatic wheeze audible on every inhale, dry and right on the mic. Instrumental: 88 BPM, swung dusty breakbeat with a thick knocking kick and a hard flat snare, a melancholy after-midnight Rhodes-and-organ soul-jazz figure sliced into a cold, menacing minor loop, walking acoustic-bass-style bottom end, tape hiss and crackle; between the rules a hoarse sampled crowd-chant voice barks the number; bare, minimal, threatening, no hook
exclude: machine-gun cadence, words piled onto one bar, breathless sprinting delivery, female voice, sung hook, auto-tuned vocal, trap hi-hat rolls
lyrics:
[Intro]
Uh. Money printer manual. Take notes.

[pause: one bar, only the Rhodes loop and kick, mic quiet]

[Rule 1]
Rule number Uno: [pause: one full beat, nothing said] never say how much you made,
doesn't matter anyway, since the gold went away.

[two-bar beat break: the MC rests while the swung break and the organ figure carry eight beats, the crowd voice calls the next number]

[Rule 2]
Number two: [pause: one full beat, nothing said] never show 'em your next move,
cut the rate for the banks, hike it when you land.

[two-bar beat break: the MC rests while the swung break and the organ figure carry eight beats, the crowd voice calls the next number]

[Rule 3]
Number three: [pause: one full beat, nothing said] never trust nobody with the press,
before Bernie gets made off face loss.

[two-bar beat break: the MC rests while the swung break and the organ figure carry eight beats, the crowd voice calls the next number]

[Rule 4]
Number four: [pause: one full beat, nothing said] never get high on your own supply,
banks took the first hit, now the rent's sky-high.

[two-bar beat break: the MC rests while the swung break and the organ figure carry eight beats, the crowd voice calls the next number]

[Rule 5]
Number five: [pause: one full beat, nothing said] never print where you sleep,
never let them owe the oats you reap.

[two-bar beat break: the MC rests while the swung break and the organ figure carry eight beats, the crowd voice calls the next number]

[Rule 6]
Number six: [pause: one full beat, nothing said] no credit? Forget it,
let the junkie know you better forget that.

[two-bar beat break: the MC rests while the swung break and the organ figure carry eight beats, the crowd voice calls the next number]

[Rule 7]
Seven, [pause: one full beat, nothing said] and nobody says it out loud:
keep your money and your assets apart, not in one crowd.

[two-bar beat break: the MC rests while the swung break and the organ figure carry eight beats, the crowd voice calls the next number]

[Rule 8]
Number eight: [pause: one full beat, nothing said] hold none of it yourself,
debase 'em till the numbers go through.

[two-bar beat break: the MC rests while the swung break and the organ figure carry eight beats, the crowd voice calls the next number]

[Rule 9]
Nine's the one they'd rather you skipped: [pause: one full beat, nothing said]
keep the auditors out, sporadic trips and you out.

[two-bar beat break: the MC rests while the swung break and the organ figure carry eight beats, the crowd voice calls the next number]

[Rule 10]
Number ten: [pause: one full beat, nothing said] no consignment, cash up front, that's law,
they took the bailout in stride and they ain't paid it all.

[pause: one bar, the loop thins to kick and bass]

[Outro]
And the fix, from the future? No hand on the printer.

[beat plays on two bars, then stops dead]

[End]
